title: Research: certification-mark program models
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. licensing-model.md proposes a 'RAS-certified' certification mark held by a neutral body, so that only third-party-tested gear carries it.
objective: Compare existing certification-mark programs for safety gear (e.g., helmet, climbing and child-seat programs): holder structure, lab accreditation, fees, revocation and recalls, with sources.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 5 programs compared with sources
Options for who could hold the RideBelt/RAS mark
Clear note that this is not legal advice
Every factual claim has a cited, working source link; estimates are labelled as estimates
